episodes.187054: From January 12th through January 17th, a slow moving trough brought Flash Flooding and high wind gusts at times for all islands of American Samoa. WSO Pago Pago recorded 10.58 inches of rain throughout the six day span. Flash flooding occurred on numerous occasions.
episodes.187332: Very cold temperatures led to rapid ice formation on rivers.  Localized flooding due to ice jams occurred along portions of the Kankakee River.
episodes.187519: A series of weather systems brought impactful winter weather to the area with light snow developing across north central Montana, becoming more widespread across the region. Dangerously cold wind chills persisted along the Hi-Line. Warming temperatures elsewhere led to ice jamming, resulting in flooding concerns across portions of the Treasure State. ||** Isolated 9 inch snowfall report 6 WSW Forestgrove left out of report.||Re-assessed Aug/Sept of 2024 due to timing inconsistencies.
episodes.187661: A cold front caused flooding and wind damage over portions of the islands.
episodes.187685: A thunderstorm moving offshore produced a strong wind gust in Melbourne.
episodes.188622: A surface trough moving through produced gusty winds across portions of the Chesapeake Bay.

events.narrative: The main road through the village of Leloaloa was covered in at least 6 inches of water and flowing into residential areas due  to flash flooding. Rainfall estimated over 2 inches in the region between 2:50 and 4:50 PM. Local Red Cross reports of one family from a residential home needed assistance.

Flash flooding caused the roadway between WSO Pago Pago and the airport covered with water and significant ponding on surrounding properties. WSO Pago Pago recorded 2.15 inches of rain between 02:50 PM and 04:50 PM.

A video from social media shows significant flooding from a stream flowing from Mt. Alava to the village of Vatia. Video shows areal flooding of properties from the overflowing stream. Rainfall is estimated around 3 inches in the area between 2:50 and 4:50 PM. The local red cross office reports there was a family in need of assistance in the region.
Significant ponding on the Fagaima road caused water to flow onto residential properties due to flash flooding. Estimated rainfall over the region is between 2:50 PM and 4:50 PM is 3 inches.
An ice jam upstream from the Starved Rock Lock and Dam extending upstream to near Naplate caused minor flooding near Ottawa.

Reported ice jam along the Beaverhead River northeast of Dillon, resulting in flooding along Laknar Lane, Pond Drive, and Park Street in North Dillon. Mitigation using hay bales prevented the flooding waters to move into another flood basin; however, some homes were still flooded in this area.
South Kihei Road was closed between Kaonoulu and Ohukai. The west bound lanes were closed due to heavy flooding. Emergency managers reported a swift water rescue.
